entities.summary:
Mehmed II, commonly known as Mehmed the Conqueror, was the sultan of the Ottoman Empire twice, from August 1444 to September 1446 and then later from February 1451 to May 1481. 


Born in 1432 in Trabzon, Ottoman Empire, Mehmed II was the son of Sultan Murad II and his second wife, Valide Sultan. He became the sultan at the age of 12 after his father's death and ruled until his own death. Mehmed II's reign is notable for his military campaigns, including the conquest of Constantinople in 1453, which marked the end of the Byzantine Empire and the beginning of the Ottoman Empire's dominance in Eastern Europe. Mehmed II also oversaw the construction of the Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul, which became one of the most iconic landmarks of the Ottoman Empire. 


Mehmed II's legacy extends beyond his military conquests and architectural achievements. He played a significant role in shaping the Ottoman Empire's relations with Europe, particularly during the reign of Pope Nicholas V. Mehmed II also established the Ottoman Empire as a major power in the Mediterranean, rivaling the power of the Byzantine Empire. Mehmed II's reign marked the beginning of the Ottoman Empire's decline, as the empire began to fragment and lose its territorial control. 


Mehmed II's reign was also marked by significant cultural and religious developments. He supported the spread of Islam and encouraged the translation of Christian texts into Turkish. Mehmed II also patronized the arts and architecture, commissioning many notable buildings and monuments during his reign. Mehmed II's reign is often seen as a turning point in Ottoman history, marking the beginning of the Ottoman Empire's rise to power and its eventual decline.
